We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+{20}^{∘} & ={60}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}, & \, & \, & 4x+{20}^{∘} & ={300}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & ={60}^{∘}-{20}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & 4x & ={300}^{∘}-{20}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} \\ 4x & ={40}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} & \, & \, & 4x & ={280}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘} \\ x & ={10}^{∘}+n\cdot {90}^{∘} & \, & \, & x & ={70}^{∘}+n\cdot {90}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x={10}^{∘}$ and $x={70}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x={100}^{∘}$ and $x={160}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x={190}^{∘}$ and $x={250}^{∘}.$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x={280}^{∘}$ and $x={340}^{∘}.$

All other integer values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$ 

So, in ascending order, the solutions are

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={10}^{∘},\, & {x}_{2} & ={70}^{∘},\, & {x}_{3} & ={100}^{∘}, & {x}_{4} & ={160}^{∘},\, \\ {x}_{5} & ={190}^{∘},\, & {x}_{6} & ={250}^{∘},\, & {x}_{7} & ={280}^{∘}, & {x}_{8} & ={340}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
